sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page teme1252 (references: Bennett 1983 'Adamawa-Eastern: problems and prospects'; Boyd & Pasch 1988; Meek 1931 'Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria'; Blench Atlas). Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.
sources.note: Only subclassification/overview references are attached; no grammar, phonology or sketch is recorded for Teme.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Teme language' and 'Yendang languages'; Wikidata Q3913994; Joshua Project tdo; Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz (Kleinewillinghöfer), site and site search for 'Teme'.
sources.note: No descriptive source cited anywhere; Wikipedia cites only Ethnologue (4,000 speakers, 1995) and Blench's Maya wordlists / Atlas. The Mainz project has no Yandang/Teme page and its search for 'Teme' returns only unrelated hits.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 2020 edition (version 11 September 2020). Cambridge: self-published (McDonald Institute address). Entry 436 'Teme', printed p. 93.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry reads in full: '436. Teme / 1.A Temme / 3. Adamawa State, Mayo Belwa and Fufore LGAs / 5. no data. Adamawa–Ubangi: Adamawa: Mumuye–Yendang group: Yendang subgroup'. Per the front matter (3.8 Documentation status) 'no data' means the author could find no linguistic data at all on the language. The sister language Waka (entry 475, p. 100) is likewise 'no data'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition III. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (= Glottolog ref 108472, 'no date [1999]', the only Glottolog reference for Teme). Entry 422 'Teme', printed p. 81.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives only alternate name (Temme), location (Adamawa State, Mayo Belwa and Fufore LGAs) and classification; no Source(s)/Refs line at all.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009 (pdf dated 29 May 2009). The Maya [Yendang] languages: wordlists collected by Barau Kato and Zachariah Yoder, analysis by Roger Blench. 15 pp. unpublished ms., Cambridge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Teme. Wordlists (tone-marked) only for Bali, Kpasham, Yoti and Yandang; Teme appears solely as a node in the classification tree on p. ii ('Bali-Kpasham | Waka-Yendang-Yoti | Teme | Gengle-Kugama-Kumba'). Intro: 'The Yandang languages as a whole are barely known.. there is no published evidence for such a classification.' No stress or tone discussion.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [2004]. List of Adamawa languages. Unpublished ms., rogerblench.info.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Teme is item 5 under VI. Mumuye-Yendang > ii. Yendang, with no data or references.

sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond. 1999 [as cited by Blench 2009]. Lexical material on Yandang (exact title not seen); and Boyd, Raymond. 1989. Adamawa-Ubangi. In J. Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 178-215. Lanham: UPA.

sources.note: Boyd is the only linguist besides Blench cited as having Yendang-group data; the 1989 chapter contains general remarks on Adamawa tone systems but nothing Teme-specific is expected.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1979. A comparative study of the Mumuye dialects (Nigeria). Berlin: Reimer (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A/14).

sources.note: Closest published phonological/comparative work on the Mumuye-Yendang group; covers Mumuye lects (mentions Yoti), not Teme. Useful only as a family-level proxy for tone; not a Teme source.

sources.citation: Kato, Barau & Zachariah Yoder (SIL Nigeria). c. 2008-2009. Sociolinguistic survey of the 'Maya' (Yendang-cluster) peoples, Adamawa State (cited as 'Kato (2009)' in Blench Atlas 2020 s.v. Yendang and as the source of the wordlists in Blench 2009).

sources.note: Only known fieldwork project that targeted the Yendang cluster in the 2000s; a survey report might contain a Teme wordlist or intelligibility data, though a stress statement is unlikely.
